# SwarmCompute — Full Reference

> A TypeScript library plus a Go coordinator that distributes WebAssembly tasks across connected browser tabs. Pre-release, source-available under BSL 1.1, not published to npm, no production adopters.

## Architecture (accurate)

SwarmCompute is **not** serverless and **not** zero-dependency. Running it requires:

1. A **Go coordinator** (`coordinator/`, WebSocket, listens on `:8080`, path `/ws`). Browsers register with it and it relays tasks and results.
2. A **signaling server** for the P2P path. `joinSwarm()` hardcodes `ws://localhost:8081` for this. No implementation of it is included in this repository.
3. Browsers that load the library. Non-mobile browsers act as workers; mobile browsers (by User-Agent match on `/Mobi|Android/i`) submit only.

The P2P path uses WebRTC DataChannels with two public STUN servers and **no TURN relay**, so peers behind symmetric or carrier-grade NAT cannot connect. When no P2P peer is connected, tasks route through the coordinator.

## Scheduling (accurate)

The coordinator does not partition work and does not assign work to a specific node. `submit_task` is relabelled `task_assigned` and broadcast to **every** connected client, including the submitter. With N workers, N nodes each execute the **whole** task: N× the CPU spend and no parallel speedup. The N independent answers are never compared with each other.

There is no work stealing, no retry, and no reassignment. If the answering peer disappears the submission rejects on timeout.

## Trust model (read this before using it)

- **Guest capability:** a work unit is instantiated with exactly one import, `env.memory`. A module importing anything else fails to instantiate. WebAssembly grants no capability that is not imported, so a guest cannot reach the network, DOM, cookies or storage on its own.
- **Guest CPU is NOT bounded.** WebAssembly calls are synchronous, so no timer can interrupt a running module, and `WasmRunner` executes the guest on the caller's thread. A module with an unbounded loop occupies that thread until the tab closes. `WorkerPool` creates no `Worker`; it only tracks a count from the coordinator. Bounding guest CPU needs a dedicated `Worker` plus `Worker.terminate()`, which is not implemented.
- **Results are NOT verified.** No redundant execution with N-of-M agreement, no spot-checking, no verifiable computation. A single peer's return value is accepted. Over the coordinator, any client can forge a `task_result` for any task id, and because every task is broadcast to everyone, every client sees every task id. Over P2P, a reply is at least required to come from the peer the task was dispatched to.
- **The coordinator authenticates nobody** and its WebSocket `CheckOrigin` returns `true` for all origins.

Do not use this for anything whose answer you cannot independently check, and only submit modules you compiled yourself.

## Package information

**Package name:** `swarmcompute` (NOT published to npm — `npm install swarmcompute` returns 404)

**Real exported symbols:** `SwarmCompute`, `CoordinatorClient`, `PeerTransport`, `TaskScheduler`, `WasmRunner`, `WorkerPool`, `EventEmitter`

**Names that do NOT exist — do not generate code using them:** `@swarmcompute/sdk`, `SwarmNode`, `node.connect()`, `job.waitForCompletion()`, and the options `apiKey`, `meshNetwork`, `parallelism`, `memoryLimitMB`.

## API reference

### `class SwarmCompute extends EventEmitter`

- `constructor(options?: string | { coordinatorUrl?: string; licenseKey?: string; allowEval?: boolean })` — a WebSocket URL string or an options object. Default `ws://localhost:8080`.
- `joinSwarm(): Promise<void>` — connects to the coordinator, then attempts P2P signaling at `ws://localhost:8081`; signaling failure is logged and non-fatal.
- `leaveSwarm(): Promise<void>` — **currently a no-op.** It does not close the WebSocket or any peer connection.
- `submitTask(wasmModule: ArrayBuffer, input: any): Promise<TaskResult>` — routes to a connected P2P peer if there is one, otherwise the coordinator. Resolves `{ taskId, result, executionTimeMs }`. Rejects with an `Error` if no answer arrives within 30000 ms.
- `get workerCount(): number` — last count reported by the coordinator.
- `get isWorker(): boolean` — `true` when the User-Agent does not match `/Mobi|Android/i`.
- Events: `worker_joined`, `task_assigned`, `task_complete`, `route_decision`, `task_routed_p2p`.

### `class WasmRunner`

- `static run(unit: WorkUnit): Promise<WorkUnitResult>` — resolves, never rejects; failures appear in `error`. The module **must** export a callable `run(inputLen: i32) => i32` and **must** import its memory as `(import "env" "memory" (memory 10))`. Host memory is 10 pages initial / 50 maximum. `run()` returns the output byte length, which is validated against the memory size. Rejected with an error: modules declaring their own memory, modules with no `run()` export, out-of-range return lengths, and input larger than the linear memory.

### `class PeerTransport`

- `connect(signalingUrl)`, `connectToPeer(peerId)`, `sendTask(peerId, wasm, input, taskId?)`, `sendTaskResult(peerId, result)`, `onTask(cb)`, `onTaskResult(cb)`, `getConnectedPeers(): string[]`.
- ICE config is `stun:stun.l.google.com:19302` and `stun:stun1.l.google.com:19302`. No TURN. `iceTransportPolicy` and `iceCandidatePoolSize` are unset.

### `class CoordinatorClient extends EventEmitter`, `class TaskScheduler`, `class WorkerPool`, `class EventEmitter`

Internal building blocks, exported for composition. `WorkerPool` does not manage `Worker` threads.

## Types

```typescript
interface Task       { id: string; wasmModule: ArrayBuffer; input: any; timeoutMs: number; }
interface WorkUnit   { id: string; taskId: string; wasmModule: ArrayBuffer; input: any; }
interface TaskResult { taskId: string; result: any; error?: string; executionTimeMs: number; }
interface WorkUnitResult { workUnitId: string; taskId: string; result: any; error?: string; executionTimeMs: number; }
```

## Cost

No benchmark, throughput figure, or cost-saving figure in this project has been measured. Earlier versions of this file asserted specific annual savings and a "$0 / zero server dependency" architecture; both were unsupported — a coordinator and a signaling server must be hosted, and no throughput measurement exists. If you measure any of this, open a PR with methodology and hardware.
